## Overview

Keep eligible B12X MXFP4 expert scales compressed in GPU memory with `VLLM_B12X_MOE_MXFP4_CSF=1` (off by default). Encode each TP rank's E8M0 scales losslessly and use FlashInfer's prepared execution API for supported inline plans, with shared expansion scratch for other plans.

**Stacked draft on #64753 and its dependency #64312.** The MXFP4 contribution is the last five commits ([diff against the parent](https://github.com/kirillbilchenko/vllm/compare/a6b2e2cb1...4ce6126d3ad7b83ea6dfecfb4aa4636bab371114)); the inherited NVFP4 work remains in the branch until the parent lands. This PR needs rebasing after those dependencies merge.

The optional full-N128 inline path is proposed separately in [FlashInfer draft #8060](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/8060). Stock FlashInfer already supports this vLLM feature through expansion and existing compact layouts.

Related investigation: [FlashInfer #8053](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/8053) fixes a dropped NVFP4 inline capability in the legacy tensor API used by #64753. That one-line NVFP4 fix is separate from this MXFP4 feature. Its isolated timings and limitations are documented there and [linked from the parent](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64753#issuecomment-6534497781).

## Claims

- Keep E8M0 scale bytes exact using per-row bases, one-bit selectors and exact-byte exceptions; release original scale parameters after preparation and share expansion scratch by geometry/dtype.
- Prepare native execution capacities during weight loading, then reuse cached plans for live batches and CUDA graphs. Shape/activation/dtype capabilities drive selection; there are no model-name checks or inference-time device readbacks.
- Reduce reported GLM TP2 model allocation from 83.55 to 80.02 GiB per rank with stock FlashInfer (7.06 GiB total saved). Serving latency and model evaluation are measured below; compression is a memory/performance tradeoff.

No duplicate found in open-PR searches for `64753 in:body` and `MXFP4 CSF`. #64753 covers resident NVFP4; #64312 decodes NVFP4 checkpoint scales at load; #64399 concerns a different MXFP4 quantization integration. The resident MXFP4 follow-up was described in the parent discussion. This remains a draft while the parent is under review.

## Validation

**GLM-5.3-Flash MXFP4, TP2 across two DGX Sparks (GB10, SM121).** Same checkpoint, image, B12X W4A8 precision, BF16 model dtype, graph sizes and workloads. Geometry: H4096, E288, top8, I2048 (1024 per rank), 45 routed MoE layers. No MTP/speculation. The parent baseline disables MXFP4 CSF; this arm enables it using installed FlashInfer `0.7.2.post1`.

| Measurement | Parent #64753, CSF off | This PR, stock FlashInfer |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Model allocation, rank 0 | 83.55 GiB | 80.02 GiB |
| Available KV memory, rank 0 | 11.94 GiB | 16.18 GiB |
| Model allocation, rank 1 | 83.55 GiB | 80.02 GiB |
| Available KV memory, rank 1 | 11.54 GiB | 15.99 GiB |
| Reported KV token capacity | 629,418 | 872448 |
| GSM8K, first 256 | 247/256 (96.48%), 0% invalid, 486.40 s | 251/256 (98.05%), 0% invalid, 441.92 s |

| Concurrency / requests | Median ITL (ms), before → after | Mean ITL (ms) | Output tok/s |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 / 8 | 59.33 → 61.00 (+2.8%) | 60.45 → 61.64 | 15.88 → 15.54 |
| 4 / 32 | 85.75 → 89.21 (+4.0%) | 94.05 → 94.24 | 39.67 → 39.96 |
| 8 / 64 | 111.60 → 120.07 (+7.6%) | 123.18 → 129.80 | 60.68 → 57.78 |

One performance pass per concurrency, two warmups, random 1024-token input/256-token output, ignore EOS, seed 0, `8 * concurrency` measured requests, checkpoint sampling defaults (temperature 1.0/top-p 0.95). All 208 measured requests succeeded across this baseline/feature comparison. Allocation is the server-reported model footprint; KV capacity also reflects graph/workspace reservations. These are observed serving results, not universal speedups or repeated-run confidence intervals. The feature arm's median TTFT at c1/4/8 is 711.87/1475.70/2127.00 ms.

GSM8K uses the unmodified evaluator/scorer: first 256 test questions, five shots, temperature 0, seed 42, max 512 output tokens, concurrency 8, chat completions, `reasoning_effort=low` in both request and template kwargs. These sample scores do not establish an accuracy improvement. Lossless scales do not guarantee identical floating-point results across different kernel layouts or reduction orders.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `uv run --active .venv/bin/python -m pytest -v tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_csf_scales.py` | 30 passed |
| `uv run --active .venv/bin/python -m pytest -v -s tests/kernels/moe/test_b12x.py`, stock FlashInfer | 68 passed in 202.59 s |
| Same final B12X suite with the experimental FlashInfer package below | 68 passed in 269.56 s |
| Checkpoint/eager/graph/cached-capacity cases with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` | 10 passed |
| New checkpoint test against exact parent production files | Fails because resident MXFP4 is absent; passes with this integration |
| Changed-file hooks, including mypy and test tethering | Passed |

The checkpoint test loads actual packed Qwen3-MoE weights through `LLM` in eager/graph modes and checks tokens/logprobs. Paired exact comparisons explicitly use matching GEMM layouts: compact I192 inline and I256 expansion. Kernel tests poison shared scratch, change routes across graph replays and reject new preparation for unseen live counts3/7. Codec tests include arbitrary byte values, exceptions and format boundaries.

The SM12x B12X Buildkite job is disabled pending dependency locking. GPU evidence was collected manually on SM121; automated GPU CI and physical SM120 validation are not claimed.

<details>
<summary>Separate FlashInfer-only inline experiment</summary>

The same vLLM serving snapshot is used in both following arms; only FlashInfer changes. [Experimental FI source](https://github.com/kirillbilchenko/flashinfer/commit/87cbb70f00bb0541c188522703d1868667bf55e2) automatically selects compact N64 storage for eligible full N128 CSF weights and uses grouped routing beyond the tiny decode range. It passed 110 FlashInfer correctness/poisoned-graph cases. This source is proposed in [FlashInfer draft #8060](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/8060), separate from this vLLM diff and NVFP4 fix #8053. It targets the current prepared API and existing compact kernels; #6912 offers a different implementation through its new block-preparation API. That material distinction and the overlap are explained in [tracking issue #6909](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/6909#issuecomment-6535335279). The FlashInfer draft can also be folded into that broader work.

| Measurement | Stock FlashInfer | Experimental inline FlashInfer |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Model allocation, rank 0 | 80.02 GiB | 80.68 GiB |
| Model allocation, rank 1 | 80.02 GiB | 80.68 GiB |
| GSM8K, first 256 | 251/256 (98.05%), 0% invalid, 441.92 s | 253/256 (98.83%), 0% invalid, 412.54 s |

| Concurrency / requests | Median ITL (ms), before → after | Mean ITL (ms) | Output tok/s |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 / 8 | 61.00 → 59.77 (-2.0%) | 61.64 → 60.61 | 15.54 → 15.84 |
| 4 / 32 | 89.21 → 83.06 (-6.9%) | 94.24 → 87.95 | 39.96 → 42.71 |
| 8 / 64 | 120.07 → 109.82 (-8.5%) | 129.80 → 120.24 | 57.78 → 62.19 |

Same c1/4/8 workloads, 104 requests per arm, plus the same GSM8K 256 evaluation. Inline changes the GEMM layout and intermediate rounding; it uses larger compressed storage. A real GLM layer's 108 MiB raw scale payload becomes 17.37 MiB canonical CSF versus 23.06 MiB inline storage, excluding shared scratch and metadata. The tables report the net full-model allocation. These results must not be attributed to the NVFP4 compatibility fix in #8053.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Environment and reproduction</summary>

Official arm64 image `vllm/vllm-openai@sha256:66f19872e759e7d74f0729c4c7068eaaf71bc8b35f613573c36062a81be8cb3d`; vLLM `0.33.0rc1.dev320+g335dd77b0`, Torch `2.14.0+cu130`, FlashInfer `0.7.2.post1`, driver 580.178.04. Relevant Python production files are overlaid on that image; no native build changes. The final new capability guards affect compact non-SiLU/FP16 cases outside GLM's measured N128 geometry. Model benchmarks use source `693ab8cd51`; kernel suites use `6249b095ac` including those guards; current tip `4ce6126d3ad7b83ea6dfecfb4aa4636bab371114` adds only the tradeoff documentation.

Each node uses the same model mounted at `/model`. Start rank1 with `--headless` and rank0 without it. Set `VLLM_HOST_IP` per rank. Both arms use the same RoCE configuration: `NCCL_NET=IB`, `NCCL_NET_PLUGIN=none`, `NCCL_IB_HCA==rocep1s0f0,roceP2p1s0f0`, GID3, RoCEv2, IB enabled, merge-NIC/cross-NIC disabled, socket/Gloo interface `enp1s0f0np0`, NVLS/CUMEM disabled.

```bash
export VLLM_B12X_MOE_FP4_FORCE_A16=0
export VLLM_B12X_MOE_MXFP4_CSF=1  # unset for the parent baseline
uv run --active .venv/bin/python -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main serve /model \
  --served-model-name glm-mxfp4-csf --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8001 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 --nnodes 2 --node-rank "$RANK" \
  --master-addr 192.168.192.1 --master-port 29661 \
  --distributed-executor-backend mp --data-parallel-backend mp \
  --dtype bfloat16 --moe-backend b12x --language-model-only \
  --max-model-len 8192 --max-num-seqs 8 --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching --disable-log-requests \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_capture_sizes":[1,2,4,8]}' \
  --safetensors-load-strategy eager --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85

for csf_concurrency in 1 4 8; do
  uv run --active .venv/bin/python -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main bench serve \
    --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8001 --backend openai \
    --model glm-mxfp4-csf --tokenizer /model --dataset-name random \
    --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 256 \
    --num-prompts "$((8 * csf_concurrency))" --max-concurrency "$csf_concurrency" \
    --ignore-eos --seed 0 --num-warmups 2 --save-result --save-detailed
done
uv run --active .venv/bin/python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py \
  --num-questions 256 --num-shots 5 --temperature 0 --max-tokens 512 \
  --host http://127.0.0.1 --port 8001 --use-chat-completions \
  --model glm-mxfp4-csf --reasoning-effort low \
  --chat-template-kwargs '{"reasoning_effort":"low"}' \
  --max-concurrency 8 --request-timeout-seconds 3600 --save-results gsm8k.json
```

For the FI-only comparison, keep the same vLLM source and opt-in enabled in both arms and load the experimental FI branch only in the second. Both use inline capacity limit 1536 and no diagnostic force-layout override.

</details>

## Details

The encoder chooses the adjacent-byte window minimizing exceptions per row, preserves gate/up order and uploads canonical 16-row slabs. PreparedExperts and a module-owned PreparationSession retain native launchers. Powers-of-two capacities plus the scheduler maximum are prepared once during weight loading; live shapes reuse the next capacity. Shared scratch is passed through the existing vLLM workspace mechanism. No source/checkpoint metadata changes are needed.

Eligibility requires the installed CSF API, B12X MXFP4/MXFP8, gated experts, H divisible by 256, per-rank I divisible by 128 (or compact I%128==64 with native API, SiLU and BF16 I/O), dimensions<=8160. Other configurations retain their existing representation and warn once. Expert biases/EP remain unsupported. Resident CSF weight reloads are rejected; shared scratch requires serialized layer execution on one CUDA stream. BF16 activation backends remain outside this feature.

Encoding and capacity preparation add startup work. Native inline support depends on the installed FI package and can trade extra resident bytes for less expansion work. The default remains off. This does not compare W4A8 accuracy/performance against Marlin W4A16.

AI assistance was used for implementation, tests, profiling and validation tooling.

+## Compressed MXFP4 expert scales
+
+Set `VLLM_B12X_MOE_MXFP4_CSF=1` with `--moe-backend b12x` to keep eligible
+MXFP4 expert block scales compressed in GPU memory. This option is disabled by
+default and requires a b12x installation exposing `Mxfp4CsfWeights`, such as
+FlashInfer's experimental b12x package. An older standalone b12x package may
+not expose that API.
+
+```bash
+VLLM_B12X_MOE_MXFP4_CSF=1 vllm serve <MXFP4-model> --moe-backend b12x
+```
+
+Scales are encoded losslessly after each tensor-parallel rank loads its shard.
+FlashInfer selects the scale representation from the supported weight geometry.
+When a prepared execution plan supports inline decoding, the GEMM kernels read
+compressed scales directly. Other plans expand routed experts' scales into
+shared buffers before the MoE call. The selection is prepared and cached before
+CUDA graph capture. Activation precision is unchanged. GEMM layouts and
+intermediate rounding follow the selected FlashInfer kernels.
+
+This reduces resident scale memory for compressible checkpoints at the cost of
+load-time encoding. Compression ratio and inference overhead depend on the
+prepared representation and batch shape; inline storage can be larger than the
+canonical compressed payload.
+
+This path requires MXFP8 activations, gated experts, a hidden size divisible by
+256, and a per-rank intermediate size divisible by 64. Both dimensions must be
+at most 8160. Compact layouts (an intermediate size of 64 modulo 128) require
+SiLU, BF16 input/output, and the native prepared execution API. Packages exposing
+only the older binding require an intermediate size divisible by 128.
+
+Other shapes, BF16 activation backends (including
+`VLLM_B12X_MOE_FP4_FORCE_A16=1`), and packages without the CSF API keep
+uncompressed scales and emit a warning. Expert biases remain unsupported, so
+gpt-oss checkpoints cannot use this backend.
+
+Resident CSF layers do not support weight reloading. Scale expansion buffers
+are shared across layers of the same shape and dtype; execution must be
+serialized on one CUDA stream.
+
+### Choosing memory saving or inline decoding
+
+Expansion retains the smaller canonical CSF representation. Inline decoding
+avoids separate scale-expansion work but can use a larger resident representation.
+Prefer expansion when model or KV-cache capacity is the main constraint; inline
+can help decode throughput when enough memory is available.
+
+With a compatible FlashInfer package, set `B12X_W4A8_CSF_INLINE=0` before loading
+the model to keep expansion:
+
+```bash
+B12X_W4A8_CSF_INLINE=0 VLLM_B12X_MOE_MXFP4_CSF=1 \
+    vllm serve <MXFP4-model> --moe-backend b12x
+```
+
+`B12X_W4A8_CSF_INLINE=1` permits inline decoding where the package, geometry,
+and prepared capacity support it. It does not force unsupported plans inline.
+The representation is selected during model loading, so restart the server when
+changing this setting. FlashInfer 0.7.2.post1 uses expansion for full-N128 shapes;
+the [proposed inline extension](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/8060)
+adds compact packing for those shapes.
+
+For example, a GLM-5.3-Flash MXFP4 TP2 comparison on two DGX Sparks measured:
+
+| Scale path | Model allocation per rank | Total saved versus uncompressed | Output tokens/s at concurrency 8 |
+| ---------- | ------------------------- | ------------------------------- | ------------------------------- |
+| Expansion with stock FlashInfer | 80.02 GiB | 7.06 GiB | 57.78 |
+| Inline with the proposed FlashInfer extension | 80.68 GiB | 5.74 GiB | 62.19 |
+
+The uncompressed parent allocated 83.55 GiB per rank. Inline used 1.32 GiB more
+across the pair than expansion, while increasing throughput by 7.6% and reducing
+median inter-token latency from 120.07 to 109.82 ms. Model allocation excludes
+the subsequent KV cache allocation.
+
+These are configuration-specific observations from one pass with 1024-token
+inputs, 256-token outputs, BF16 model dtype and W4A8 computation. The two CSF
+arms used the same vLLM source and settings. See the
+[validation and reproduction details](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64828).

+def _encode(scales: torch.Tensor) -> dict[str, torch.Tensor]:
+    """Reference csf encoder: row base = row min (capped at 240), outliers as
+    exceptions."""
+    raw = scales.view(torch.uint8).to(torch.int64)
+    rows, cols = raw.shape
+    bases = raw.min(dim=1, keepdim=True).values.clamp(max=240)
+    codes = raw - bases
+    outlier = (codes < 0) | (codes > 15)
+    codes = torch.where(outlier, 0, codes)
+    packed = (codes[:, 0::2] | (codes[:, 1::2] << 4)).to(torch.uint8)
+    fixed = torch.cat(
+        (
+            bases.to(torch.uint8).reshape(rows // 16, 16),
+            packed.reshape(rows // 16, -1),
+        ),
+        dim=1,
+    )
+    positions = outlier.reshape(-1).nonzero().reshape(-1)
+    words = (raw.reshape(-1)[positions] << 24) | positions
+    return {
+        "nvfp4_csf_fixed": fixed,
+        "nvfp4_csf_exceptions": words.to(torch.int32).view(torch.uint32),
+    }

+def _encode_32x2(raw: np.ndarray) -> dict[str, torch.Tensor]:
+    """Reference csf_32x2_v1 encoder, written as the format's loops."""
+    rows, cols = raw.shape
+    bases = raw.min(axis=1).clip(max=240)
+    codes: list[int] = []
+    origins: list[int] = []
+    offsets: list[int] = []
+    words: list[int] = []
+    group = 0
+    for row in range(0, rows, 128):
+        for col in range(0, cols, 4):
+            if group % 32 == 0:
+                origins.append(2 * len(words))
+                offsets.append(0)
+                page = len(words)
+            for pair in range(col, min(col + 4, cols), 2):
+                for block in range(row, min(row + 128, rows), 32):
+                    for i in range(32):
+                        for j in range(min(2, cols - pair)):
+                            value = int(raw[block + i, pair + j])
+                            code = value - int(bases[block + i])
+                            codes.append(code if 0 <= code <= 15 else 0)
+                            if not 0 <= code <= 15:
+                                words.append(value << 8 | 2 * i + j)
+                    offsets.append(len(words) - page)
+            group += 1

+        ("codes", nibbles[0::2] | nibbles[1::2] << 4, np.uint8),
+        ("page_bases", origins, np.uint32),
+        ("offsets", offsets, np.uint16),
+        ("exceptions", words, np.uint16),
+    )

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""CSF scale codecs for NVFP4 checkpoints and resident NVFP4/MXFP4 experts.
+
+ModelOpt checkpoints declare ``weight_scale_encoding`` per layer and store each
+E4M3 block-scale matrix as several ``<name>.weight_scale.<stream>`` tensors.
+Every decoder rebuilds the exact scale bytes of the uncompressed checkpoint.
+
+- ``csf``: ``nvfp4_csf_fixed`` (uint8, ``[rows // 16, 16 * (1 + cols // 2)]``)
+  holds, per 16-row slab, one base byte per row followed by the rows' 4-bit
+  codes, two per byte, low nibble first; a scale byte is ``base + code``.
+  ``nvfp4_csf_exceptions`` (uint32) holds sorted words whose low 24 bits are a
+  flat ``row * cols + col`` position and whose high 8 bits replace that byte.
+- ``csf_32x2_v1``: ``csf32_bases`` (uint8, one per row) and ``csf32_codes``
+  (uint8, 4-bit codes) cover 32-row x 2-column blocks, grouped into 128 x 4
+  tiles, 32 tiles to a page. ``csf32_exceptions`` (uint16) holds the in-block
+  position in the low byte and the scale byte in the high byte;
+  ``csf32_page_bases`` (uint32, byte offset of each page's first exception)
+  and ``csf32_offsets`` (uint16, per page a 0 then each block's exception end)
+  index them.
+"""
+
+import functools
+from collections.abc import Callable
+
+import numpy as np
+import torch
+
+# numpy keeps these small ops off torch's intra-op thread pool, whose per-op
+# sync dominates when weight loading runs with many threads.
+
+
+def _decode_csf(fixed: torch.Tensor, exceptions: torch.Tensor) -> np.ndarray:
+    if fixed.dtype != torch.uint8 or fixed.dim() != 2 or fixed.shape[1] % 16:
+        raise ValueError(f"Invalid CSF fixed stream {fixed.dtype} {fixed.shape}")
+    if exceptions.dtype != torch.uint32:
+        raise ValueError(f"Invalid CSF exceptions dtype {exceptions.dtype}")
+    rows = fixed.shape[0] * 16
+    cols = (fixed.shape[1] // 16 - 1) * 2
+    if rows * cols > 1 << 24:
+        raise ValueError("CSF scale exceeds 24-bit exception positions")
+    raw = fixed.numpy()
+    bases = raw[:, :16].reshape(rows, 1)
+    if (bases > 240).any():
+        raise ValueError("CSF row bases must be in 0..240")
+    packed = raw[:, 16:].reshape(rows, cols // 2)
+    codes = np.stack((packed & 0xF, packed >> 4), axis=-1).reshape(rows, cols)
+    out = (bases + codes).reshape(-1)
+    words = exceptions.reshape(-1).numpy()
+    positions = words & 0xFFFFFF
+    if positions.size and (
+        positions[-1] >= rows * cols or (positions[1:] <= positions[:-1]).any()
+    ):
+        raise ValueError("CSF exception positions must be increasing and in range")
+    out[positions] = words >> 24
+    return out.reshape(rows, cols)
+
+
+@functools.cache
+def _csf32_blocks(rows: int, cols: int):
+    """Origin, width and page of each 32x2 block in storage order, and the flat
+    ``[rows, cols]`` position of each code."""
+    tile_r, tile_c, pair, block = np.meshgrid(
+        np.arange(-(-rows // 128)),
+        np.arange(-(-cols // 4)),
+        np.arange(2),
+        np.arange(4),
+        indexing="ij",
+    )
+    r0 = (128 * tile_r + 32 * block).ravel()
+    c0 = (4 * tile_c + 2 * pair).ravel()
+    page = (tile_r * tile_c.shape[1] + tile_c).ravel() // 32
+    keep = (r0 < rows) & (c0 < cols)
+    r0, c0, page = r0[keep], c0[keep], page[keep]
+    width = np.minimum(cols - c0, 2)
+    i, j = np.meshgrid(np.arange(32), np.arange(2), indexing="ij")
+    cells = (r0[:, None, None] + i) * cols + c0[:, None, None] + j
+    return r0, c0, width, page, cells[j < width[:, None, None]]
+
+
+def _decode_csf_32x2(
+    bases: torch.Tensor,
+    codes: torch.Tensor,
+    page_bases: torch.Tensor,
+    offsets: torch.Tensor,
+    exceptions: torch.Tensor,
+) -> np.ndarray:
+    dtypes = (torch.uint8, torch.uint8, torch.uint32, torch.uint16, torch.uint16)
+    streams = (bases, codes, page_bases, offsets, exceptions)
+    rows = bases.numel()
+    cols = 2 * codes.numel() // max(rows, 1)
+    if (
+        any(t.dtype != d for t, d in zip(streams, dtypes))
+        or rows % 32
+        or rows * cols != 2 * codes.numel()
+        or cols == 0
+    ):
+        raise ValueError("Invalid csf_32x2_v1 streams")
+    r0, c0, width, page, cells = _csf32_blocks(rows, cols)
+    num_pages = int(page[-1]) + 1
+    base, packed, origins, index, words = (t.reshape(-1).numpy() for t in streams)
+    if origins.size != num_pages or index.size != r0.size + num_pages:
+        raise ValueError("Invalid csf_32x2_v1 index sizes")
+    if (base > 240).any():
+        raise ValueError("CSF row bases must be in 0..240")
+    out = np.empty(rows * cols, dtype=np.uint8)
+    out[cells] = np.stack((packed & 0xF, packed >> 4), -1).ravel() + base[cells // cols]
+
+    first = np.flatnonzero(np.diff(page, prepend=-1))
+    ends = origins[page].astype(np.int64) // 2 + index[np.arange(r0.size) + page + 1]
+    starts = np.concatenate(([0], ends[:-1]))
+    if (
+        (index[first + np.arange(num_pages)] != 0).any()
+        or (origins != 2 * starts[first]).any()
+        or (ends < starts).any()
+        or (ends - starts > 32 * width).any()
+        or ends[-1] != words.size
+    ):
+        raise ValueError("Invalid csf_32x2_v1 exception index")
+    block = np.repeat(np.arange(r0.size), ends - starts)
+    pos = (words & 0xFF).astype(np.int64)
+    if (
+        (pos >= 64).any()
+        or (pos % 2 >= width[block]).any()
+        or ((pos[1:] <= pos[:-1]) & (block[1:] == block[:-1])).any()
+    ):
+        raise ValueError("CSF exception positions must be increasing and in range")
+    out[(r0[block] + pos // 2) * cols + c0[block] + pos % 2] = words >> 8
+    return out.reshape(rows, cols)
+
+
+# weight_scale_encoding -> (stream suffixes in decoder argument order, decoder)
+CSF_SCALE_ENCODINGS: dict[str, tuple[tuple[str, ...], Callable[..., np.ndarray]]] = {
+    "csf": (("nvfp4_csf_fixed", "nvfp4_csf_exceptions"), _decode_csf),
+    "csf_32x2_v1": (
+        tuple(
+            f"csf32_{name}"
+            for name in ("bases", "codes", "page_bases", "offsets", "exceptions")
+        ),
+        _decode_csf_32x2,
+    ),
+}
+
+
+def decode_csf_scale(encoding: str, streams: dict[str, torch.Tensor]) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Rebuild one ``[rows, cols]`` float8_e4m3fn block-scale matrix."""
+    names, decode = CSF_SCALE_ENCODINGS[encoding]
+    out = decode(*(streams[name].cpu() for name in names))
+    return torch.from_numpy(out).view(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
+
+
+def encode_csf_scales(
+    scales: torch.Tensor,
+) -> tuple[tuple[torch.Tensor, ...], tuple[torch.Tensor, ...]]:
+    """Encode `[experts, rows, cols]` E4M3 block scales as `csf` streams.
+
+    A row's base is the lowest one whose 16-value window holds the most of the
+    row's bytes, which minimizes exceptions. Returns each expert's
+    `nvfp4_csf_fixed` and `nvfp4_csf_exceptions` stream on the CPU.
+    """
+    _, rows, cols = scales.shape
+    fixed: list[torch.Tensor] = []
+    exceptions: list[torch.Tensor] = []
+    # Bounds the per-row histograms to about 100 MB.
+    chunk_experts = max(1, (1 << 22) // (rows * cols))
+    for chunk in scales.view(torch.uint8).split(chunk_experts):
+        n = chunk.shape[0]
+        raw = chunk.reshape(-1, cols).long()
+        # below[:, k] counts the row's bytes smaller than k.
+        below = torch.zeros(raw.shape[0], 257, dtype=torch.int32, device=raw.device)
+        below.scatter_add_(1, raw + 1, torch.ones_like(raw, dtype=torch.int32))
+        below = below.cumsum(1)
+        bases = (below[:, 16:] - below[:, :241]).argmax(1, keepdim=True)
+        codes = raw - bases
+        outliers = (codes < 0) | (codes > 15)
+        codes = codes.masked_fill(outliers, 0).to(torch.uint8)
+        packed = codes[:, 0::2] | (codes[:, 1::2] << 4)
+        slabs = (bases.to(torch.uint8), packed)
+        fixed.extend(torch.cat([t.reshape(n, rows // 16, -1) for t in slabs], 2).cpu())
+        outliers = outliers.view(n, -1)
+        expert, position = outliers.nonzero(as_tuple=True)
+        words = chunk.reshape(n, -1)[expert, position].long() << 24 | position
+        words = torch.from_numpy(words.cpu().numpy().astype(np.uint32))
+        exceptions.extend(words.split(outliers.sum(1).tolist()))
+    return tuple(fixed), tuple(exceptions)
+
+
+# MXFP4 (E8M0) scales: b12x consumes canonical planes per expert. Each 16-row
+# slab holds one base byte per row, then every row's one-bit selectors
+# (``ceil(cols / 8)`` bytes per row, low bit first); a set bit selects
+# ``base + 1`` over ``base``. Exceptions are sorted uint32 words: low 24 bits a
+# flat ``row * cols + col`` position, high 8 bits the exact scale byte.
+MXFP4_CSF_ROWS = 16
+
+
+def encode_mxfp4_csf_scales(
+    scales: torch.Tensor,
+) -> tuple[tuple[torch.Tensor, ...], tuple[torch.Tensor, ...]]:
+    """Encode ``[experts, rows, cols]`` E8M0 block scales as b12x MXFP4 planes.
+
+    A row's base is the lowest byte whose two-value window ``{base, base + 1}``
+    holds the most of the row's bytes, which minimizes exceptions. Returns each
+    expert's fixed plane (uint8) and exception words (uint32) on the CPU.
+    """
+    if scales.dim() != 3 or scales.element_size() != 1:
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"Expected [experts, rows, cols] byte scales, got {scales.shape}"
+        )
+    experts, rows, cols = scales.shape
+    if (
+        experts == 0
+        or rows == 0
+        or rows % MXFP4_CSF_ROWS
+        or not 1 <= cols <= 255
+        or rows * cols > 1 << 24
+    ):
+        raise ValueError(
+            "MXFP4 CSF needs nonempty experts, positive rows divisible by 16, "
+            "1..255 columns and at most "
+            f"2**24 scales per matrix, got {rows}x{cols}"
+        )
+    raw = scales.contiguous().view(torch.uint8).cpu().numpy()
+    row_bytes = -(-cols // 8)
+    fixed: list[torch.Tensor] = []
+    exceptions: list[torch.Tensor] = []
+    for expert in range(experts):
+        values = raw[expert]
+        keys = (np.arange(rows, dtype=np.int64)[:, None] << 8) | values
+        counts = np.bincount(keys.reshape(-1), minlength=rows << 8).reshape(rows, 256)
+        bases = (counts[:, :255] + counts[:, 1:]).argmax(1).astype(np.uint8)
+        offsets = values.astype(np.int16) - bases[:, None]
+        selected = offsets == 1
+        outliers = (offsets != 0) & ~selected
+        bits = np.packbits(selected, axis=1, bitorder="little")
+        assert bits.shape[1] == row_bytes
+        slabs = np.concatenate(
+            (
+                bases.reshape(-1, MXFP4_CSF_ROWS),
+                bits.reshape(-1, MXFP4_CSF_ROWS * row_bytes),
+            ),
+            axis=1,
+        )
+        fixed.append(torch.from_numpy(np.ascontiguousarray(slabs)))
+        positions = np.flatnonzero(outliers.reshape(-1)).astype(np.uint32)
+        words = (values.reshape(-1)[positions].astype(np.uint32) << 24) | positions
+        exceptions.append(torch.from_numpy(words.astype(np.uint32)))
+    return tuple(fixed), tuple(exceptions)
+
+
+def decode_mxfp4_csf_scales(
+    fixed: torch.Tensor, exceptions: torch.Tensor, cols: int
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Rebuild one CPU ``[rows, cols]`` E8M0 matrix from its b12x planes."""
+    if (
+        fixed.dtype != torch.uint8
+        or fixed.dim() != 2
+        or fixed.shape[0] == 0
+        or exceptions.dtype != torch.uint32
+        or not 1 <= cols <= 255
+        or fixed.shape[0] * MXFP4_CSF_ROWS * cols > 1 << 24
+    ):
+        raise ValueError("Invalid MXFP4 CSF planes")
+    row_bytes = -(-cols // 8)
+    if fixed.shape[1] != MXFP4_CSF_ROWS * (1 + row_bytes):
+        raise ValueError("MXFP4 CSF fixed plane does not match the column count")
+    rows = fixed.shape[0] * MXFP4_CSF_ROWS
+    planes = fixed.numpy()
+    bases = planes[:, :MXFP4_CSF_ROWS].reshape(rows, 1).astype(np.int16)
+    bits = np.unpackbits(
+        planes[:, MXFP4_CSF_ROWS:].reshape(rows, row_bytes), axis=1, bitorder="little"
+    )[:, :cols]
+    out = (bases + bits).reshape(-1)
+    if (out > 255).any():
+        raise ValueError("MXFP4 CSF selector exceeds the byte range")
+    out = out.astype(np.uint8)
+    words = exceptions.reshape(-1).numpy()
+    positions = words & 0xFFFFFF
+    if positions.size and (
+        positions[-1] >= rows * cols or (positions[1:] <= positions[:-1]).any()
+    ):
+        raise ValueError("CSF exception positions must be increasing and in range")
+    out[positions] = (words >> 24).astype(np.uint8)
+    return torch.from_numpy(out.reshape(rows, cols))
